title: 18th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:00 with 34 members present, adopted the minutes of sittings 14 to 17, and the chair declined an urgent matter from the Kendhoo member because it did not meet the Rules of Procedure. Three presidential nominations (the Privatization and Corporatization Board chair, a non-resident ambassador to Azerbaijan and a Civil Service Commission member) were sent to committees. Members then began the preliminary debate on a motion by Dr Ahmed Shamheed asking members' views on the government and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) acting against the 2025 budget and fiscal laws, centred on the MMA buying land from HDC in Hulhumale'. MDP members backed the motion and warned of inflation and credit rating risks, while PNC members called it political and said no money is being printed; the debate was still running when this part ends, with no vote. This part continues the debate on an urgent motion from Dr Ahmed Shamheed (MDP, South Hulhumale') asking MPs to state their view on the government's and the Maldives Monetary Authority's actions that go against the passed 2025 budget, which in practice became an argument over whether the government is printing money and how past governments handled debt. A speech by the PNC parliamentary group leader that began in the previous part ends, then six more members speak, with PNC members saying the government has not printed money and MDP members saying such moves must go through the Majlis. After a recess, one more member spoke and the motion's sponsor was not in the chamber when the debate closed. In the vote, 10 members voted yes and 46 no, so the motion was not accepted, and the sitting ended. The text layer is garbled in places, so some figures quoted in speeches are not repeated here.

items.title: Preliminary debate on the motion by Dr Ahmed Shamheed on government and MMA actions said to depart from the 2025 budget and the MMA, public finance and fiscal responsibility laws
items.outcome: debated; continues into part 2, no vote in this part

items.title: Urgent motion by Dr Ahmed Shamheed on government and Monetary Authority actions against the 2025 budget (debate continued)
items.outcome: debated; a recess ran from 11:02 to 12:00; debate closed because the sponsor was not in the chamber

items.title: Vote on accepting the urgent motion
items.outcome: not accepted, 10 yes, 46 no, 0 abstain (56 voted)

items.title: Speaker closes the sitting
items.outcome: sitting closed; date of next sitting to be announced later

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Moved the motion, saying MMA land purchases from HDC and government borrowing from the MMA conflict with the budget and fiscal laws.
Closing: said he could not get written answers through the Finance Committee, and that any money printing should come to parliament first.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order that the mover's person, not the motion, was being discussed; the chair did not accept it as a point of order.
Said the MMA buying about 22 hectares of land amounts to money printing, risking prices, the dollar rate and credit rating.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said the MMA should not be buying land and that printing money without parliament's approval breaks the law.
Warned that prices, taxes and the credit rating would suffer, and asked the government to be responsible.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Called the motion false, saying the Finance Minister told him no request was sent to the MMA.
Said the President has repeatedly said money will not be printed and cited unfinished Addu City development.
Said the motion is not based on anything that has happened, since no money has been printed under this government.
Asked MDP members, including the member for Kendhoo, whether they opposed money printing and the suspended finance law in the previous term.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Called the motion groundless and politically driven, pointing to the MDP-era printing of about MVR 8.8 billion.
Said the MMA law lets it buy land and that the MMA and government are separate bodies.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the motion cites no evidence and that development projects should not be obstructed.
Criticised the mover's party record on debt and used the debate to defend the President's projects.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said the MDP government printed MVR 8.8 billion over four years under Covid, and asked who was accountable then.
Said the central bank's debt had grown and criticised the mover for leaving the chamber.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Defended Covid-era spending as a response to closed tourism and stimulus support for workers.
Said the MMA had been drawn under political influence and questioned the land price paid.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said the economy is fragile and blamed past borrowing, but that the MMA governor's performance is not part of the motion.
Noted some economists say limited printing could help the economy and urged responsible handling.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Said the motion's headline gives no details of what the MMA is alleged to have done.
Cited the rufiyaa's fall and high debt under MDP rule and asked the opposition to offer policies.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said the motion is serious, and that the MMA buying 22 hectares of land would effectively create money.
Warned of effects on the dollar rate and credit rating and said the central bank should not be politicised.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said the motion is political, linked to the mover's announced presidential primary bid.
Said the previous government left heavy debt and the present one is honouring obligations without printing money.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the motion's wording is weak and rests on no solid facts.
Asked opposition members to stop causing public fear and respect the laws governing the MMA.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Called the motion a waste of the House's time.
Said the MMA has legal authority over its decisions and the Finance Ministry sent it no request to print money.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Described the motion as a campaign stunt after the mover's presidential bid announcement.
Said printing money happened under the previous government, not this one.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said printing money is not a religious or criminal matter but must follow the law, and the MMA Act allows land purchases only in set cases.
Said the credit rating and business conditions have not improved and disputed the claimed debt figures.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Called the motion based on suspicion, saying there is no evidence in it.
Cited about MVR 60 billion borrowed under the previous government and said printing is not planned (speech continues in part 2).

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Said the economy is fine and the problem is how the government manages it, citing large hiring at state companies and the earlier GST increase.
Said he and his group worry the government is borrowing and creating money in ways that members and the public are not told about.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Said MDP members who bring urgent motions are wasting the Majlis's time and criticised their record on borrowing and on suspending the finance law during Covid.
Said the current government repaid a USD 100 million loan without printing money and backed the PNC group leader's remarks.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Said the motion has no basis because the government has not printed money, and that a USD 100 million loan was repaid last month without printing.
Contrasted MVR 8.8 billion printed under the previous government with current repayments, and asked MDP members to support island and local council candidates.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said money created by the Monetary Authority is mostly digital, not banknotes, and could weaken the rufiyaa if not handled carefully.
Asked that any money creation be brought to the Majlis under the law and explained to the public.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the motion, saying it asks what the Majlis thinks and that the law allows printing money under set conditions and Majlis approval.
Asked how many people had received the direct subsidy the budget promised from April.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Said the government has not announced printing money and explained that creating money, physical or electronic, tends to raise inflation.
Said international bodies have advised against it and hoped the policy of not printing money would continue.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 14 to 17 of the first session were accepted without amendment.
The urgent matter from the Kendhoo member was not accepted for debate.
The Privatization and Corporatization Board chair nomination was referred to the State-Owned Enterprises Committee.
The non-resident ambassador to Azerbaijan nomination was referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The Civil Service Commission member nomination was referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The Majlis did not accept Dr Ahmed Shamheed's urgent motion: 10 voted yes and 46 voted no, with 29 votes needed.
The debate on the motion was closed after the speaking list ran out and the member who tabled it was not in the chamber.
The Speaker closed the sitting and said the date of the next sitting would be announced later.

votes.what: Whether to accept Dr Ahmed Shamheed's urgent motion on the actions of the government and the Maldives Monetary Authority against the 2025 budget (minutes list 93 members in total, 57 present, 56 voted)
